prompt.context_jp: 夏祭りの提灯が並ぶ川辺に、笛と太鼓の音___ゆるやかに流れていた。
prompt.prompt_jp: 夏祭りの提灯が並ぶ川辺に、笛と太鼓の音___ゆるやかに流れていた。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle that fits this descriptive opening sentence.

feedback.correct_en: This is a descriptive scene-setting line introducing the sounds as new information to the reader — が marks that fresh perceived subject.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would treat the sounds as an already-established topic, which doesn't fit an opening scene. を would wrongly make the sounds a direct object.

contrast_examples.jp: 遠くで花火が上がった。
contrast_examples.en: Fireworks went up in the distance. (new information)

contrast_examples.jp: その花火は毎年恒例だ。
contrast_examples.en: Those fireworks are an annual tradition. (established topic)

prompt.context_jp: 森若___休むというのは、部内でも珍しい出来事である。
prompt.prompt_jp: 会社の経理綱領を誰よりも忠実に守る森若___休むというのは、部内でも珍しい出来事である。
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle fits inside this noun-modifying clause?

feedback.correct_en: Inside a relative/nominalized clause ending in というのは, the embedded subject takes が, not は. は is reserved for the main-clause topic.
feedback.incorrect_en: は inside this subordinate clause would clash with the outer というのは topic marking.

prompt.context_jp: 「えっ 森若さん___？ 珍しいですね」
prompt.prompt_jp: えっ 森若さん___？ 珍しいですね
prompt.prompt_en: Mabuki has just said Moriwaka is taking a sick day. Pick the particle.

feedback.correct_en: The speaker is reacting with surprise to Moriwaka as the newly-identified subject of 'taking off' — exhaustive/identificational が ('Moriwaka, of all people?').
feedback.incorrect_en: は would sound like continuing an established topic rather than reacting with surprise.

contrast_examples.jp: 森若さんは元気ですよ。

prompt.context_jp: 「弟さん___ お電話がありました」
prompt.prompt_jp: 弟さん___ お電話がありました
prompt.prompt_en: Reporting who the call came from.

feedback.correct_en: から marks the source of the phone call — 'from her younger brother'.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would make the brother a topic, not the source. で (location/means) doesn't fit a phone caller.

contrast_examples.en: A letter came from my mother.
I made a call at the station.

prompt.context_jp: 昨日の21時48分 森若さん___ 共有フォルダーを 開いた履歴があったんです
prompt.prompt_jp: 森若さん___ 共有フォルダーを開いた履歴があったんです
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle fits in this noun-modifying clause (log evidence)?

feedback.correct_en: The clause modifies 履歴 — inside such a relative clause the subject takes が, not は.
feedback.incorrect_en: は inside a noun-modifying clause is unnatural here; it would compete with the main-clause topic.

contrast_examples.en: the book he wrote (relative clause → が)
He wrote a book. (main clause → は)

prompt.context_jp: 「私___日曜日に 会社に行っておりません」
prompt.prompt_jp: 私___日曜日に 会社に行っておりません
prompt.prompt_en: Sanako is denying the accusation. Pick the particle.

feedback.correct_en: She is contrasting herself against the accusation ('as for me, I did not...') — classic contrastive/topic は.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would sound like she's identifying the subject of a new fact, not denying an accusation about herself.

contrast_examples.en: I did not go (contrasting with the accusation).

prompt.context_jp: 「大丈夫です 私___何もしてませんから」
prompt.prompt_jp: 私___何もしてませんから
prompt.prompt_en: Sanako reassures Taiyo. Pick the particle.

feedback.correct_en: She establishes herself as the topic ('as for me, I didn't do anything') — は fits reassurance about one's own innocence.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would sound like identifying who did nothing out of a group, which isn't the point here.

contrast_examples.en: I'm the one who doesn't know. (exhaustive)

prompt.context_jp: 「でも日曜日の夜 彼女___家にいたんです」
prompt.prompt_jp: でも日曜日の夜 彼女___家にいたんです
prompt.prompt_en: Tagura defends Sanako against suspicion. Pick the particle.

feedback.correct_en: He's contrasting Sanako's whereabouts against the accusation ('she, at least, was at home') — contrastive は.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would identify her out of a group as the one at home, which misses the defensive contrast.

contrast_examples.en: She was at home (contra the accusation).

contrast_examples.jp: 誰が家にいた？―彼女がいた。

prompt.context_jp: 君の名前で 共有フォルダーのアクセス___あり その資料が流出した
prompt.prompt_jp: 君の名前で 共有フォルダーのアクセス___あり
prompt.prompt_en: The executive is stating a fact. Pick the particle.

feedback.correct_en: 〜がある is the standard existence pattern; が introduces 'access' as the existing fact.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would require an already-known access event to contrast; this is a newly-presented accusation.

prompt.context_jp: 「有本さん___ 毎週水曜日 早退されてますね」
prompt.prompt_jp: 有本さん___ 毎週水曜日 早退されてますね
prompt.prompt_en: Sanako notes a pattern about Arimoto. Pick the particle.

feedback.correct_en: She establishes Arimoto as the discussion topic ('as for Arimoto, she leaves early every Wed') — は.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would sound like a new identification rather than describing a habitual pattern of a known person.

prompt.context_jp: 浮かれた気分もつかの間、沙名子の手からスマートフォン___滑り落ちた。
prompt.prompt_jp: 沙名子の手からスマートフォン___滑り落ちた
prompt.prompt_en: Describe the sudden event. Pick the particle.

feedback.correct_en: A sudden event with the phone newly introduced as the actor — が.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would make the phone an established topic, which doesn't fit this abrupt narrative moment.

contrast_examples.jp: そのコップは割れない。

prompt.context_jp: 「電源___ 入らないっすね」
prompt.prompt_jp: 電源___ 入らないっすね
prompt.prompt_en: Taiyo on the broken phone. Pick the particle.

feedback.correct_en: The power is a newly-tested, newly-failing attribute of the fallen phone — が in the 〜が入らない pattern.
feedback.incorrect_en: は could appear in a contrastive reading, but here it is a bare observation of a failed state — が is more natural in this exclamation.

contrast_examples.jp: 電源は入るけど画面がつかない。
contrast_examples.en: Power's on, but the screen won't (contrast).

prompt.context_jp: あの 私___ 到着するまで 絶対に誰にも言わないでください
prompt.prompt_jp: 私___ 到着するまで 絶対に誰にも言わないでください
prompt.prompt_en: Minase on the phone, inside a 〜まで clause.

feedback.correct_en: Inside a subordinate 〜まで clause, the subject takes が.
feedback.incorrect_en: は inside this subordinate temporal clause would be unnatural; は tends to appear in the main clause.

prompt.context_jp: 「あっ 震えてるじゃないすか」—「これは… ___です」
prompt.prompt_jp: これは… ___です
prompt.prompt_en: Sanako covers up her shivering with a joke. Choose the word.

feedback.correct_en: 武者震い (a warrior's thrill of anticipation) is the deadpan joke Sanako uses to deny she's cold.
feedback.incorrect_en: 貧乏揺すり is nervous leg-jiggling; 身震い is a shudder of fear/disgust — neither carries the self-mocking bravado.

prompt.context_jp: 「大丈夫 大丈夫 “人の噂も___”」
prompt.prompt_jp: 人の噂も___
prompt.prompt_en: The classic Japanese proverb used to console Sanako.

feedback.correct_en: The real proverb is 人の噂も七十五日 — rumors only last 75 days. Later in the chapter Mayu misquotes it as 四十九日 (which is a Buddhist memorial), which is the running joke.
feedback.incorrect_en: 四十九日 is a funeral rite period, not the proverb. 百日 is not the fixed form.

prompt.context_jp: 二兎を追う者は___をも得ず。
prompt.prompt_jp: 二兎を追う者は___をも得ず
prompt.prompt_en: Complete the proverb Sanako recalls.

feedback.correct_en: The set proverb is 二兎を追う者は一兎をも得ず — chase two hares, catch neither (not even one).
feedback.incorrect_en: 二兎 would repeat the first clause; 何 breaks the fixed form.

contrast_examples.jp: 二兎を追う者は一兎をも得ず
contrast_examples.en: He who chases two hares catches neither.

prompt.context_jp: 「では あなたは ___を かぶったままでいいと？」
prompt.prompt_jp: あなたは___をかぶったままでいいと？
prompt.prompt_en: Mabuki asks if Sanako is content to accept false blame.

feedback.correct_en: ぬれぎぬを着る/かぶる is the set idiom for 'being falsely accused'.
feedback.incorrect_en: かさ (umbrella) fits the verb but not the meaning; 面目 doesn't collocate with かぶる in this sense.

prompt.context_jp: 「確かに ___接待の可能性もあります」
prompt.prompt_jp: ___接待の可能性もあります
prompt.prompt_en: The accounting team suspects a fraudulent entertainment expense.

feedback.correct_en: 空接待 (kara-settai) is the business-fraud term: billing an entertainment expense that didn't actually happen as claimed.
feedback.incorrect_en: 偽接待 and 裏接待 are not the established term; the chapter uses 空接待 specifically.

contrast_examples.jp: 空接待で経費を落とす
contrast_examples.en: to expense a fake entertainment outing
a fake business trip (same 空 pattern)

prompt.context_jp: 「これを機に 経理部の___化を 本格的に進めようと思います」
prompt.prompt_jp: 経理部の___化を本格的に進めよう
prompt.prompt_en: The executive announces a cost-cutting move.

feedback.correct_en: アウトソーシング化 = outsourcing — hiring an external accounting firm to replace in-house staff, as explained in the next lines.
feedback.incorrect_en: ブランディング/マーケティング have no connection to replacing accounting workers.

contrast_examples.jp: 業務をアウトソーシングする

prompt.context_jp: 「熱 ちょっと今日 会社 ___ほうが いいかもしんないっす」
prompt.prompt_jp: 今日 会社 ___ほうがいい
prompt.prompt_en: Taiyo suggests Sanako skip work.

feedback.correct_en: 〜た方がいい (past-form + ほうがいい) is the standard suggestion/advice pattern.
feedback.incorrect_en: 休む (plain) softens the advice too much and sounds less natural here. 休んで (te-form) doesn't combine with ほうがいい.

contrast_examples.en: You'd better not take time off.

prompt.context_jp: 「___をすれば なんとやら…」(有本が入ってきた瞬間)
prompt.prompt_jp: ___をすれば なんとやら
prompt.prompt_en: Sanako half-mutters a proverb as Arimoto appears.

feedback.correct_en: 噂をすれば影 ('speak of the devil') — the idiom uses 噂.
feedback.incorrect_en: 話 and 陰口 don't fit this fixed proverb.

contrast_examples.en: to talk behind someone's back (different idiom)

prompt.context_jp: 「___いたしました 私 麻吹が承りました ボス」
prompt.prompt_jp: ___いたしました
prompt.prompt_en: Mabuki's business-polite phone acknowledgment.

feedback.correct_en: 承知いたしました is the standard humble business acknowledgment to a superior or client.
feedback.incorrect_en: 了解しました is more casual among colleagues and considered less polite upward. 分かりいたしました is ungrammatical.

prompt.context_jp: Which rendering of the narrator's reflection sounds more natural?
prompt.prompt_en: Pick the more natural phrasing for 'this time walking a step behind Taiyo felt comforting.'

choices.text: 太陽の一歩後ろを歩くこの時間が、なぜか心地よかった。
太陽の一歩後ろを歩くこの時間は、なぜか心地よかった。

feedback.correct_en: The sentence introduces this specific moment as a newly-noticed, remarkable thing — が highlights the subject of the sudden feeling.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would treat 'this time' as an already-established topic being commented on, flattening the discovery tone that fits the narrative.

contrast_examples.en: This scenery (right now) is beautiful. (new impression)

contrast_examples.jp: この景色は毎日見ている。
contrast_examples.en: This scenery, I see every day. (established topic)

prompt.context_jp: Sanako apologizes for not answering the door.
prompt.prompt_en: Which line sounds more natural in this apology?

choices.text: ごめんなさい、スマホが壊れてしまって。
ごめんなさい、スマホを壊れてしまって。

feedback.correct_en: 壊れる is intransitive, so the thing that broke is marked with が.
feedback.incorrect_en: を requires a transitive verb like 壊す. 壊れる + を is ungrammatical.

prompt.context_jp: Mabuki tells Sanako that doubting her is a waste of time.
prompt.prompt_en: Which version sounds more natural as Mabuki's catchphrase?

choices.text: 疑うだけ時間のムダです。タイム イズ マネー。
疑うだけ時間がムダします。タイム イズ マネー。

feedback.correct_en: 〜のムダ (a waste of X) is the fixed noun phrase. '時間のムダ' = waste of time.
feedback.incorrect_en: ムダする is not a verb; the noun form with の is required.

prompt.context_jp: Sanako gratefully declines the team's offer to hunt the real culprit.
prompt.prompt_en: Which phrasing sounds more natural in Sanako's polite refusal?

choices.text: お気持ちはうれしいけど、大丈夫です。
お気持ちがうれしいけど、大丈夫です。

feedback.correct_en: は contrasts their kind feelings with her reluctance to pursue the matter — the natural setup for a polite 'but'.
feedback.incorrect_en: が here loses the contrastive nuance that pairs with the けど clause.

contrast_examples.jp: 気持ちはうれしいけど断る。
contrast_examples.en: The thought is appreciated, but I decline.

contrast_examples.jp: 気持ちがうれしくて泣いた。
contrast_examples.en: I was so happy at the thought that I cried. (new emotion, no contrast)
